elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.11: examinations may not "(b) be conducted more than once in any twelve (12) month period" (redaction replaced with an express twelve-month cap).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.11 inserts only "upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice"; to reach the preferred level the period must read thirty (30) days.
No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in rendered 6.11-6.13; the clause is silent on timing of access.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 6.11 retains "an independent public accounting firm of nationally recognized standing designated by Harpoon and reasonably acceptable to AbbVie".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: 6.13 obliges the Parties to cause only the "Audit Expert" (the Section 6.12 dispute firm) to sign a confidentiality agreement, and binds the receiving Party under Article 9; the Section 6.11 auditing firm is not expressly placed under confidentiality obligations (6.11 only limits what it may disclose to Harpoon).

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site or remote-review preference is stated in rendered 6.11.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.11 shifts cost to AbbVie where "the audit reveals an underpayment exceeding ten percent (10%)" — 10%, not the preferred 5% threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: 6.11 permits the firm only "to audit the books and records maintained pursuant to this Section 6.11"; no systems, remote-access or on-premises network access right is granted anywhere in the clause.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.11(b): "be conducted more than once in any twelve (12) month period" — frequency cap now fixed rather than redacted.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.11: "upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" gates AbbVie's obligation to permit the audit.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.11: "the cost of this audit shall be borne by Harpoon, unless the audit reveals an underpayment exceeding ten percent (10%) of the reported amounts, in which case AbbVie shall bear the cost"; the alternative undefined "or [***]" cost-shifting trigger was removed so the 10% underpayment test is the sole exception.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: all three numeric terms (twelve-month frequency cap, fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, Harpoon-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%) now appear in operative language in Section 6.11, not merely in the comment.

The preferred level fails on four elements — notice is 15 rather than 30 days, no business-hours limitation, no off-site-where-possible language, and the cost-shift threshold is 10% rather than 5%; the Section 6.11 auditing firm is also not expressly bound by confidentiality (6.13 covers only the Section 6.12 Audit Expert and the receiving Party). If the preferred position is pursued, amend the notice to thirty (30) days, add "during AbbVie's normal business hours and, where reasonably practicable, off-site", change the threshold to five percent (5%), and extend 6.13's confidentiality-agreement requirement to the Section 6.11 accounting firm.

Minimality holds: the edits fill three previously redacted/open parameters and delete only the second, undefined "or [***]" cost-shifting trigger, whose retention would have left the cost element defeasible on an unspecified ground. Favourable retained language (independent nationally recognised firm reasonably acceptable to AbbVie, books-and-records-only scope, limited-disclosure restriction, carve-outs (a) and (c)) is untouched; no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures were added.

Intent is preserved: Section 6.12's Audit Expert cost-allocation mechanic still operates through the retained "Except as provided below" lead-in in 6.11, so there is no contradiction, dangling cross-reference or undefined term created by the edit.
Section 6.11 is correctly identified as the only audit right running against us; the Section 3.8.5/3.8.6 inspection rights run in our favour and are properly left unflagged.
